record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: unbounded balanced vertices from four planar boundary points
record.original_question: For every integer B at least 1, does there exist a finite connected embedded geodesic net in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and at least B balanced vertices, with straight multiplicity-one edges, no self-intersections or crossings except at common endpoints, no edges between unbalanced vertices, and balanced vertices satisfying the zero-sum unit-tangent condition? Can this already be achieved when the four unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2.2. There exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with 4 unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (Moreover, we will not be surprised if this assertion is already true in the case when the set of unbalanced vertices coincides with the set of vertices of a square).

artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. Recent work (2025) constructs an irreducible geodesic net in the plane with four boundary (unbalanced) vertices having 25 balanced vertices, improving the previous record of 16, but no construction giving arbitrarily many balanced vertices is known, nor a proof that such nets cannot exist. The analogous question for three boundary vertices has been resolved (at most one balanced vertex), in contrast to the four-vertex case.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: a geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices that has 25 balanced vertices ... increasing the previously known maximum from 16 to 25
status_evidence.claim: Progress toward the conjecture; current best construction has 25 balanced vertices, conjecture of arbitrarily many is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: For three boundary vertices, there can be at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous three-boundary-vertex problem is solved, highlighting that the four-vertex conjecture is still open.
